speaker: संजय उवाच
hindi: संजय ने धृतराष्ट्र से कहा: हे भरतवंशी राजा! अर्जुन के ऐसा कहने पर भगवान श्रीकृष्ण ने उस श्रेष्ठ रथ को दोनों सेनाओं के ठीक बीच में ले जाकर खड़ा कर दिया।
english: Sanjaya said to the king, “O descendant of Bharata, when Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep, had spoken like this, Krishna, the Lord of the senses, drew up the finest chariot right between the two armies.”
deeper: This verse is a short, quiet moment. Nothing loud happens. Krishna simply listens and does exactly what Arjuna asked. The Lord of the whole universe is sitting in the charioteer’s seat, a humble friend who is ready to serve. Krishna does not argue or hurry Arjuna. He gives him the space to look for himself.

Notice the two names. Arjuna is called Guḍākeśa, the one who has conquered sleep, meaning alert and disciplined. Krishna is called Hṛiṣhīkeśa, the master of the senses. A person who has a master of the senses beside them is in good company. When our eyes, ears and feelings pull us in many directions, a wise guide helps us stay steady.

The chariot now stands in the middle, where Arjuna can see both sides. Soon he will see his own teachers and relatives there, and his heart will tremble. That is when the real teaching of the Gita begins. Sometimes we must stop in the middle of things and look honestly at the situation. Only then can we ask for the right guidance.
words: Krishna, the Lord of the senses
by Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep
background: The two great armies, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, stood facing each other at Kurukshetra. Conch shells had been blown, and the soldiers were ready (1.12–1.19). Arjuna, with Krishna as his charioteer, looked at the Kaurava warriors standing ready with their weapons (1.20).

Then Arjuna made a request. He asked Krishna, whom he called Achyuta, to place the chariot between the two armies (1.21). He wanted to look carefully at the warriors he would have to fight (1.22–1.23). In this verse, Sanjaya tells the blind king Dhritarashtra that Krishna did exactly that.
lessons: Arjuna asked for a moment to look at the situation before the fight began, and a calm pause helps us too.
Krishna did not argue or hurry Arjuna. He listened and helped.
Stand where you can see clearly
From the middle, Arjuna could see both sides, and we understand problems better when we look at all of them.
Krishna is the master of the senses, so we can ask for help to keep our eyes, ears and feelings steady.
The Lord of the universe sat as a charioteer and served his friend with love.
examples: Two teams in your gully are arguing about whether a batter was out. You say, “Wait, let’s all stop and look at what really happened.” That pause saves the match.
Before starting the question paper, Ananya takes a deep breath and reads all the questions once. Then she decides where to begin.
Rohan feels upset after a fight with his friend. His elder cousin does not scold him. He listens quietly and then helps him think.
Two sisters both want the same toy. Their mother makes them sit together so each can say what she feels.
Before crossing the busy road on her cycle, Meera stops at the edge and looks both ways. She goes only when she can see clearly.
Aarav’s mind is racing with TV, games and chatter. He sits quietly for two minutes with his eyes closed and feels steady again.
The school captain, Kabir, helps the little ones carry their bags. He never thinks the job is too small for him.
Sana is unsure whether to tell the teacher about a mistake. She asks her grandfather, who listens carefully before he advises her.

story.title: Ishaan in the Middle of the Field
paras: On a Sunday evening in Pune, Ishaan’s colony cricket match stopped suddenly. Two groups stood on opposite sides of the ground, both shouting. “He was out!” “No, he wasn’t!” Everyone was angry, and the game was about to end in a fight.

Ishaan was the youngest player, but he walked to the middle of the ground between the two groups. He said, “Please, everyone, let me listen to each side, one at a time.” At first nobody wanted to wait. Then one by one they went quiet.

Standing in the middle, Ishaan could see everyone’s face. He heard the bowler’s side, then the batter’s side. He saw that the ball had bounced strangely, so each team had seen something different. He suggested that the batter play again, and everyone agreed.
That evening his grandfather smiled and said, “You did what a good friend does. You stopped, you listened and you saw clearly.” Ishaan felt proud, and the game began again with laughter.
story.moral: Lesson: When things get heated, stop for a moment, stand where you can see everything clearly, and listen before you act.

quiz.q: Who is called Hṛiṣhīkeśa in this verse?
quiz.x: Hṛiṣhīkeśa means the Lord of the senses, and it is a name of Krishna.

quiz.q: Where did Krishna place the chariot?
quiz.x: At Arjuna’s request, Krishna placed the best chariot in the middle of the two armies.

quiz.q: What does the name Guḍākeśa tell us about Arjuna?
o: He was the conqueror of sleep, alert and disciplined
quiz.x: Guḍākeśa means one who has conquered sleep, which shows Arjuna was alert and disciplined.

quiz.q: What can we learn from Krishna’s action in this verse?
o: A good friend listens and helps us see clearly
quiz.x: Krishna listened to Arjuna and calmly did what he asked, so he could see the situation.

reel.hook: What if the wisest thing to do is simply stop?
reel.lesson: Pause, stand in the middle, and look clearly before you act.
reel.caption:
Krishna stopped the chariot right between two armies so Arjuna could see clearly. 🛞
Before you react in anger, try a pause. 🙏
What will you pause for today?
